name: Crucible HeatWall Forge Apron MK-6
description:
A heavy split-front forge apron favored by Tier 2 foundry workers and Shelf scrap-smelters alike. The outer face is thick ceramic-fiber mat bonded to a carbonized kevlar weave, deep char-gray with heat-bloom discoloration patterns across the chest and lap from prior use. The inner contact layer is moisture-wicking aramid fleece.

Adjustable ceramic buckles at neck, waist, and thigh allow fast don/doff. The lower half splits at a central seam for mobility. A built-in tool channel runs along the right hip. Designed to be worn over standard workwear.
functionality: Rated to 1,200°C radiant exposure. Split-front lower half preserves full leg mobility at the forge. Tool channel accommodates tongs, rods, or a small extinguisher. Ceramic buckles don't conduct heat. Apron edges are triple-riveted to resist slag splash tear-through.
what_it_says: Someone who works close enough to molten metal to know exactly how hot it runs.
story_hooks: The char pattern on a particular apron matches the blast signature of a smelter explosion that officially never happened.
A Shelf forger has been using their apron's tool channel to move something other than forge equipment between shifts.
The ceramic buckles on a batch of MK-6s are counterfeit — they conduct heat at exactly the wrong moment.
